samples.xml_description: Implement a data width conversion circuit that converts 8-bit data input to 16-bit data output. Clock signal used for synchronous operation. Active-low reset signal. Defined as 0 for reset and 1 for reset signal inactive. Input signal indicating the validity of the input data. 8-bit input data to be converted. Output signal indicating the validity of the output data. 16-bit output data resulting from the width conversion. Input data width. Output data width. data_out register is updated on the positive edge of the clock signal (posedge clk) or the negative edge of the reset signal (negedge rst_n). Reset condition: When the reset signal is active (negedge rst_n), the data_out register is cleared to 0. !rst_n Width conversion condition: If the input data is valid (valid_in) and the flag signal is active, the data_out register is updated by concatenating the contents of the data_lock register (8 bits) and the data_in register (8 bits) to form a 16-bit output. valid_in && flag data_lock register is updated on the positive edge of the clock signal (posedge clk) or the negative edge of the reset signal (negedge rst_n). Reset condition: When the reset signal is active (negedge rst_n), the data_lock register is cleared to 0. !rst_n Width conversion condition: If the input data is valid (valid_in) and the flag signal is inactive, the data_lock register is updated with the input data. valid_in && !flag flag register is updated on the positive edge of the clock signal (posedge clk) or the negative edge of the reset signal (negedge rst_n). Reset condition: When the reset signal is active (negedge rst_n), the flag register is cleared to 0. !rst_n Width conversion condition: If the input data is valid (valid_in) and the flag signal is inactive, the flag register is set to 1. valid_in && !flag Reset flag condition: If the input data is valid (valid_in) and the flag signal is active, the flag register is cleared to 0. valid_in && flag Implement a data width conversion circuit that converts 8-bit data input to 16-bit data output. The module provides two output ports: valid_out, which indicates the validity of the output data, and data_out, which represents the converted 16-bit data output. The first arriving 8-bit data should be placed in the higher 8 bits of the 16-bit data output. The valid_out and data_out signals are generated in the next clock cycle after the two data inputs. When there is only one data input, valid_out and data_out are not generated immediately. Instead, they wait for the arrival of the next data input to complete the concatenation of the two data inputs before generating valid_out and data_out.
